predecessors.name: Nationalist Spain (Spanish Nationalists)
predecessors.text: the Nationalist zone of the civil war, whose rebel regime Franco headed from 1 October 1936

predecessors.name: Second Spanish Republic
predecessors.text: the last Republican territory, conquered in the first months of 1939

successors.name: Kingdom of Spain
successors.text: Spain proper and the Canary Islands, under King Juan Carlos I

successors.name: Morocco
successors.text: the Spanish Sahara, whose administration Spain gave up after the Madrid Accords of 14 November 1975

ledger.x: 1 April 1939: Franco's victory makes Spain a single Francoist state.
1947: Spain is declared a kingdom without a king.
7 April 1956: Spain gives up the northern protectorate.
1 April 1958: Spain cedes the Cape Juby strip.
1 April 1958: the Ifni War ends with the Treaty of Angra de Cintra; Spain keeps Ifni and the Sahara.
12 October 1968: Spanish Guinea becomes Equatorial Guinea.
14 November 1975: Spain agrees to leave the Sahara.
20 November 1975: Franco dies and the regime ends.

wars.name: Ifni War
wars.outcome: Spain lost the Cape Juby strip by the Treaty of Angra de Cintra (1 April 1958) and was reduced in Ifni to the city's perimeter; Ifni itself was ceded on 5 January 1969.

wars.name: Green March and Madrid Accords
wars.outcome: Spain agreed on 14 November 1975 to withdraw from the Sahara; Morocco took control after the Green March.

certainty.note: Spain's land frontiers and provincial boundaries, the 1956 and 1958 Moroccan cessions and the 1968 and 1969 handovers rest on treaties or independence acts; the interior borders of the Spanish Sahara and the Cape Juby strip were colonial…
